{{short description|French biologist}}
{{Infobox scientist|known_for={{hlist|work with [[meiofauna]]|discovery of ghost-larva}}|occupation=biologist|fields=meiofauna}}
'''Jeanne Renaud-Mornant''', Born Jeanne Renaud, Jeanne Renaud-Debyser before her second marriage (8 August 1925 Vellexon &ndash; 18 September 2012, Paris) was a French biologist specialising in [[meiofauna]].

==Biography==

Jeanne Renaud-Mornant began her career in 1951 and quickly became interested in meiofauna, a fauna compartment defined by [[Molly F. Mare|Mare]] in 1942<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Mare|first1=Molly F.|title=A study of a marine benthic community with special reference to the micro-organisms|journal=[[Journal of the Marine Biological Association of the United Kingdom]]|date=October 1942|volume=25|issue=3|pages=517–554|doi=10.1017/S0025315400055132|url=http://plymsea.ac.uk/1212/1/A_study_of_a_marine_benthic_community_with_special_reference_to_the_micro-organisms.pdf}}</ref> consisting of small benthic metazoans smaller than a millimetre in size. She obtained a [[Fulbright scholarship]] in 1953 to continue her studies in Florida, and obtained her doctoral thesis at the Sorbonne in 1961.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Renaud-Debyser|first1=Jeanne|title=Recherches écologiques sur la faune interstitielle des sables. Bassin d'Arcachon, île de Bimini, Bahamas|journal=Suppléments de la Revue Vie et Milieu|volume=15|pages=1–157|date=1963|language=French}}</ref> Soon after, she participated in the first international conference on meiofauna in Tunis<ref name="Hommage">{{cite journal|last1=Boucher|first1=Guy|last2=Lasserre|first2=Pierre|title=Hommage à Jeanne Renaud-Mornant|journal=Zoosystema|date=December 2012|volume=34|issue=4|pages=661–671|doi=10.5252/z2012n4a1|s2cid=85642186|language=French|doi-access=free}}</ref> and became increasingly involved in the scientific community by contributing to the creation of the [[International Association of Meiobenthologists]] that she chaired in 1976-1977<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.meiofauna.org/officers.html|title=International Association of Meiobenthologists &#124; Association Officers}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> and participating in the editorial board of the official newsletter of the IAM: ''Psamonalia''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.meiofauna.org/psammona.html|title=International Association of Meiobenthologists &#124; Psammonalia|access-date=2016-03-29|archive-date=2015-10-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151006193057/http://www.meiofauna.org/psammona.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>  She was particularly noted for her work with [[Tardigrada]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Truesdale|first1=Frank|title=History of Carcinology|date=1993|publisher=[[CRC Press]]|isbn=9789054101376|page=182}}</ref>

In 1967, her work caused her to be asked by the [[National Museum of Natural History (France)|National Museum of Natural History]] in Paris to assume charge of the national collection of "Vers libres" ("Free worms")<ref name="Hommage"/> in which Renaud-Mornant added in 1986, the meiofauna section<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mnhn.fr/fr/collections/ensembles-collections/invertebres-marins/meiofaune |title=Méiofaune {{!}} Muséum national d'Histoire naturelle |website=www.mnhn.fr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140411025101/http://www.mnhn.fr/fr/collections/ensembles-collections/invertebres-marins/meiofaune |archive-date=2014-04-11}} </ref> that is today a full collection consisting of specimens of free-living marine nematodes of [[Gastrotricha]], [[Kinorhyncha]], [[Tardigrades]], [[Turbellaria]], [[rotifers]], [[annelids]], and various minor groups such as [[Loricifera]]. She also participated in the staging of the meiofauna space of the [[:fr:Grande galerie de l'Évolution|Gallery of Evolution]].<ref name="Hommage"/>

In 1986, Renaud-Mornant discovered a reduced type of [[larva]] known as a "ghost-larva".<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Heiner|first1=Iben|title=''Rugiloricus bacatus'' sp. nov. (Loricifera ‐Pliciloricidae) and a ghost‐larva with paedogenetic reproduction|journal=Systematics and Biodiversity|date=June 2008|volume=6|issue=2|pages=225–247|doi=10.1017/S147720000800265X|s2cid=85855659}}</ref>

A recognised morphologist,<ref name="Hommage"/> Jeanne Renaud-Mornant also participated in many activities in the areas of eco-physiology, and phylogeny of meiofauna. She described many species of mystacocarides and gastrotrichs and 56 species, 15 genera and five new families and families in tardigrades ([[Coronarctidae]], [[Euclavarctinae]], [[Florarctinae]] ...).

== Some taxa named in her honour ==
* ''[[Sphaerosyllis renaudae]]'' Hartmann-Schroder, 1958
* ''[[Paracharon renaudae]]'' Coineau, 1968
* ''[[Stilestrongylus renaudae]]'' Durette-Desset, 1970
* ''[[Chromaspirina renaudae]]'' Boucher, 1975
* ''[[Renaudcypris]]'' McKenzie, 1980
* [[Renaudcyprinae]] McKenzie, 1980 
* ''[[Renaudarctus]]'' Kristensen & Higgins, 1984
* [[Renaudarctidae]] Kristensen & Higgins, 1984
* ''[[Syringolaimus renaudae]]'' Gourbault & Vincx, 1985
* ''[[Inanidrilus renaudae]]'' Erséus, 1985
* ''[[Thaumastoderma renaudae]]'' Kisielewski, 1988
* ''[[Parastygarctus renaudae]]'' Grimaldi de Zio, D’Addabbo Gallo, Morone De Lucia & Daddabbo, 1987
* ''[[Rugiloricus renaudae]]'' Kristensen, Neves & Gad, 2013
